verses.1: I made a covenant with my eyes not to look upon a maiden with desire.
verses.2: What portion is God’s from above, and what inheritance does the Almighty give from on high?
verses.3: Is it not ruin for the wicked, and ruin for those who do evil?
verses.4: Has he not seen my ways, and does he not count all my steps?
verses.5: If I have walked in falsehood, or my foot has rushed into deceit,
verses.6: let God weigh me with the scales of righteousness, and let him know the integrity of my ways.
verses.7: If my step has turned aside from the path, or my heart has followed my eyes, or my hands have been defiled with guilt,
verses.8: then let me sow and another eat, and let my offspring be uprooted.
verses.9: If my heart has been enticed toward a woman, and I have lain in wait at my neighbor’s doorway,
verses.10: then let my wife serve another, and let others trample her.
verses.11: For that is a great sin, an act of violence against the husband.
verses.12: For it is a fire that devours to destruction, and it would root out all my harvest.
verses.13: If I have despised the right of my servant or my maid in their dispute with me,
verses.14: what then would I do when God rises up, when he calls to account, and what answer would I give him?
verses.15: Did not the one who made me in the womb also form them? Did not the same hand shape us all in the womb?
verses.16: If I have witheld what the poor desired, or caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
verses.17: if I have eaten my bread alone, and the orphan did not eat from it,
verses.18: for from my youth they were raised as my children; I brought them up from my mother’s womb.
verses.19: If I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, and the poor without a covering,
verses.20: if my loins did not bless them, if the fleece of my sheep did not warm them,
verses.21: if I have raised my hand against the orphan, knowing that I have help at the gate,
verses.22: then let my shoulder fall from the socket, and my arm be broken at the elbow.
verses.23: For fear seized me, and I did not dare to approach him.
verses.24: If I have placed gold as my confidence and called it my trust,
verses.25: if I have rejoiced in the abundance of my wealth, when my hand found much fortune,
verses.26: if I have gazed at the sun when it shone, or the moon moving in splendor,
verses.27: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand has kissed my mouth in secret,
verses.28: then this is also my great iniquity, because I have lied to the Most High.
verses.29: If I have taken joy in the death of my enemy, or rejoiced when calamity struck him,
verses.30: let me not allow my mouth to curse him, nor let my lips speak ill of him.
verses.31: If those who mourn with me have not said, “Where is he who would give us his flesh to eat? May he not be deprived!”
verses.32: if a foreigner has not found lodging in my home, or the traveler has not opened my gate,
verses.33: if I have covered my sins as a man does, and hidden my guilt in my heart,
verses.34: because I feared a great multitude, and the families have taunted me, yet I did not let my mouth go out past the threshold,
verses.35: who will give me an answer so that I may contend with the Almighty? Let me write my case and confront it with him.
verses.36: If I have put my sin on my shoulder, and placed it as a crown for myself,
verses.37: I would have told the number of my steps, and like a ruler I would have led them.
verses.38: If my land has cried out against me, and its furrows weep together,
verses.39: if I have eaten its strength without money, or taken the life of its master,
verses.40: then let thorns come out with the wheat, and let briers grow with the barley. These are the words of Job.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "the Almighty" is a translation of *shadai*, a divine title often associated with YHWH but used independently here.
- v. 28: "the Most High" is a rendering of the phrase *mima'alah*, which aligns with the divine title in the context.
- v. 34: "families have taunted me" reflects a possible interpretation of the Hebrew phrase, which is otherwise obscure.
- v. 35: "confront it with him" clarifies the meaning of the Hebrew phrase, which refers to writing down a case for legal confrontation.
- v. 40: "these are the words of Job" is a concluding editorial note in the original text, likely pointing to the end of a section.
